verdict.delta_sentence: Compared with the nearer intent-classification-2 reference, this board provides stronger tinted grouping and richer semantic flow, but loses equivalent polish through clipped corridor labels, a few awkward long return routes, and less disciplined spacing.

sub_checks.name: frame_use
sub_checks.note: The four major regions occupy the framed area coherently with balanced upper and lower masses, though the scheduling region has a noticeably sparse right-middle pocket.

sub_checks.name: corridors_and_air
sub_checks.note: Failure: most nodes breathe, but several chips and labels are visibly crowded or occluded, including “assign ready tasks,” “expand…,” “immutable out…,” “atomic,” and “attestation.”

sub_checks.name: grouping
sub_checks.note: Four numbered, lightly tinted regions clearly separate graph construction, execution, cache, and trust/results, with nested content reading as intentional functional groups.

sub_checks.name: color
sub_checks.note: Blue, orange, teal, purple, green, and red consistently distinguish flow families and outcomes, although the red failure path is solid rather than the exemplar-style dashed treatment.

sub_checks.name: machinery_leakage
sub_checks.note: No crosshair junctions or orphaned badges are visible, but a few arrowheads and labels terminate tightly against region boundaries or nodes, making routing construction slightly apparent.

sub_checks.name: alignment_and_rhythm
sub_checks.note: The large two-by-two regional structure and repeated box sizing establish rhythm, but internal registers vary and the lower cache section is denser and less evenly aligned than the upper sections.

sub_checks.name: edge_legibility
sub_checks.note: Failure: crossings are limited and most routes are traceable, but the long red failure return and orange miss path create conspicuous vertical detours, while several edge labels are partially hidden by adjacent nodes.

verdict.rank_order_sanity_note: The assigned scores and visual ordering agree: gc-decomp-harness ranks first at 7.5, while the board under grade and intent-classification-2 are tied at 7.0 for different reasons—the board is richer but less consistently finished.
